From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>

Subject: Juniper MAP: throughput acceptance & costing — next steps

Hi Alex / Samantha —

Thanks again for the run yesterday. I put together an updated MAP (attached) that scopes the performance acceptance criteria, the evaluation runbook, and the close timeline. Key highlights: 

- Acceptance targets (canonical): sustained QPS >= 300 for 30+ minutes, sustained tokens/sec >= 45,000 (client tokenization), TTFT median < 350 ms, p95 < 600 ms, concurrency support to 8 concurrent live sessions without tail latency regression.
- Test window: Redwood will run two 60-minute sustained runs (canary + acceptance) on Mon/Tue next week, Juniper to observe via shared dashboard.
- Unit economics: baseline estimate $0.00036 per input token (including batching & KV cache), aiming to optimize to $0.00030 with quantization + batching adjustments (details in section 4 of the MAP).
- Deliverables: benchmarking_results_may09.csv (raw metrics), summary one-pager, and a short runbook for triggering emergency fallback to smaller model variants.

Action items for Juniper:
1) Confirm the prompt set and tokenization method we should use for the sustained runs (attach representative samples if different from the set in the MAP).
2) Confirm account access for the dashboard: we need at least two observers (Alex + Samantha) to be invited to the acceptance workspace.
3) Confirm billing/contact for any overage or one-off validation credits — we can offer a $5k trial credit tied to acceptance signoff, to be applied to the first month.

I attached the MAP (Juniper_MAP_v1.2.pdf) and the initial benchmarking plan. Rishi and Priyom are looped in on execution and costing notes.

If that aligns, we'll kick off the canary run Monday 09:00 PT and share telemetry.

Thanks,
Monica

Alex — thanks for the sample and the questions. Quick answers and execution plan below.

- Tokenization: Redwood accepts raw text and will run Juniper's tokenizer in our pre-processing step. For parity we can also accept pre-tokenized payloads if you prefer — either works. For the MAP we'll use Juniper's tokenizer (v2) to keep billed units aligned to production.

- Prompt stratification: yes — we'll stratify by bucket (short: <128 tokens, medium: 128–512, long: >512). The acceptance run will run each bucket for an independent sustained window and report combined + per-bucket metrics.

- Credits: the $5k credit is applied conditionally on successful acceptance signoff (i.e., meeting the acceptance targets in the MAP). If the run fails but we demonstrate reproducible mitigation steps, we can apply a smaller validation credit — we'll treat that case-by-case.

Execution timeline (proposed):
- Monday 2027-05-10 09:00 PT: Canary run (15 min per bucket, 45 min total) — observers invited.
- Tuesday 2027-05-11 10:00 PT: Acceptance run (60 min sustained per bucket) — observers invited.
- Tuesday 2027-05-11 15:30 PT: Readout call + signoff.

I've scheduled the runs and attached the runbook and a blank results CSV (benchmarking_results_may09.csv). Monica — Priyom and I will own the execution and the unit economics reconciliation.

Rishi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-11T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Juniper MAP: throughput acceptance & costing — run results + econ summary

Alex / Samantha / Monica —

Results from the acceptance run (summary below). Full raw CSV attached (benchmarking_results_may09.csv) and the brief readout deck is on the Drive link.

Run configuration: Juniper tokenizer v2, prompt buckets (short/medium/long), Redwood dedicated inference instance (mixed A100/RTX pool), standard batching policy (adaptive), KV cache enabled.

Summary metrics (acceptance run — aggregated across buckets):
- Sustained QPS (tokens/sec basis): 325 QPS equivalent (sustained tokens/sec median = 48,200) over 60 minutes.
- TTFT (time-to-first-token): median = 310 ms, p95 = 520 ms, p99 = 780 ms.
- Concurrency: system supported 8 concurrent live sessions with stable latency for the full 60-minute window. We observed acceptable degradation when stress-testing to 12 concurrent sessions (latency p95 rose to ~920 ms after 12 minutes of sustained load).
- Tail behavior: long-prompt bucket showed higher p99 (1.1s) for peaks; recommend envelope-sizing to minimize long-sequence parallelism or a model-variant fallback for >1024-token contexts.

Unit economics (measured, not yet optimized):
- Measured cost per input token (including infra, compute, and amortized overhead): $0.000341
- Estimated optimized cost with quantization + aggressive batching: $0.000298
- Estimated monthly run cost at Juniper target (steady 300 QPS sustained 24/7): ~$24,000/month (compute only, excludes storage/ingestion) — detailed line items in CSV.

Acceptance: by the MAP thresholds we hit sustained QPS and TTFT median targets. p95 is within the MAP upper bound for short/medium prompts; long prompts have elevated p99 tail — flagged as a residual risk with suggested mitigations in the runbook (attached).

Next steps we propose: 
1) Juniper signoff on acceptance (simple reply OK).
2) If accepted, finalize contract appendix for Dedicated pool sizing and commit tier (we'll attach committed pricing that maps to the optimized unit economics).
3) If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute deep-dive with infra to walk through tail mitigation (recommended).

Attachments: benchmarking_results_may09.csv, redwood-runbook-throughput.md

Thanks all — Priyom and I will draft the contract appendix and the pricing reconciliation.

Rishi
